First, I had to watch my stepbrother for a week at the beginning of the school year. My dad and his mom went on a trip to help her parents with something. When I got back to school, I eventually got annoyed with having to click on my profile each time I started a game and each time I went to the eShop. So, I just deleted his profile. Now, this early morning, I got on the train to go to my dad's for Thanksgiving. I usually go home to my mom's, but she and my stepdad are going to see his family, and I'm not up for going on a plane trip. Anyway, I brought my Switch again for the train ride. Just a little while ago, my stepbrother picked it up to start playing and came into the kitchen, where I was talking with my dad, freaking out because his Zelda save was gone and he wanted me to help him fix it. When I told him I deleted it, he started crying. Not full-on crying, but his eyes were watery a little and red. Now he's holed up in his room. My dad thinks it was mean of me to delete it because I know my stepbrother was enjoying playing it. I didn't think it was a big deal since I usually never bring my Switch over when I visit. So, is it right or wrong for me to delete his profile? I need to think about this carefully. First, I need to consider the reasons behind my actions. I made the profile for him to help him stay occupied while I studied, which was kind of a good intention. But then, when I got back to school, I got annoyed with having to switch profiles every time I used the Switch. That seems like a minor inconvenience compared to the emotional impact it had on my stepbrother. I also need to think about the consequences of my actions. Deleting his profile caused him to lose his progress in Zelda, which made him upset. My dad thinks it was mean, and I can see why he feels that way. It seems like I didn't consider how much he might care about his progress and the time he spent playing. On the other hand, I didn't think it was a big deal because I usually don't bring my Switch over when I visit. But in this case, I did bring it, and my stepbrother was using it. So, maybe I should have communicated with him before deleting his profile. If I had talked to him about my annoyance and found a solution together, like setting up a different profile or finding another way to manage the Switch, it might have gone better. I also need to think about the bigger picture. Relationships are important, and actions that seem small to me can have a big impact on others. It's important to consider other people's feelings and perspectives, especially in a family setting where trust and respect are crucial. In the future, I should think about how my actions might affect others before making decisions that could upset them. Communication is key, and taking the time to discuss issues can prevent misunderstandings and hurt feelings. So, in conclusion, while my intention was to manage my Switch usage, the way I handled it by deleting his profile without discussing it first was not considerate of my stepbrother's feelings and the impact it would have. It would have been better to communicate and find a solution together rather than acting unilaterally.
